items.summary: The Trump administration is proceeding with plans to deport some Afghan refugees back to Afghanistan despite concerns they could face Taliban persecution, according to multiple reports. Dozens have been detained in Louisiana and over 150 people are expected to be affected. The move has raised humanitarian and legal concerns.

items.summary: The Department of Justice has moved to isolate ballots in Alaska ahead of the state's ranked-choice general election on Tuesday, as part of an ongoing criminal investigation into whether two candidates sharing the name 'Dan Sullivan' could confuse voters. The race features Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan and Democratic former Rep. Mary Peltola, and is expected to determine Senate control.

items.summary: The US has approved the sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine valued at $2.1 billion, according to multiple reports. The evacuation marks a significant humanitarian development in the ongoing war.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio pulled the plug on the photo op after about one-third of countries objected. The cancellation underscores deep diplomatic fractures over Russia's war in Ukraine.

items.summary: Andhra Pradesh is preparing for a second cyclone threat just days after Cyclone Arnab devastated the region. A depression over the southeast Bay of Bengal is expected to intensify into a cyclone by November 1. State officials have been ordered to maintain high alert, monitor the system every six hours, and expedite restoration works in cyclone-affected areas.

The Ninth Circuit stayed a district court order, leaving the FY 2027 program suspended while litigation continues. The decision affects millions of prospective applicants worldwide seeking green cards through the lottery mechanism.

The midterm outcome could determine whether Democrats provide legislative checks on visa-limiting measures.

The company is working to replenish customer funds and has frozen affected assets. North Korean hackers are suspected of orchestrating the attack, which raised questions about crypto wallet security and exchange safeguards.

cards.title: Attention residue slows everything down
cards.insight: When you switch tasks, your mind doesn't follow immediately—it leaves fragments of the previous task running in the background. This 'residue' means you're never fully focused on the new task, forcing your brain to waste energy reconciling competing priorities.
cards.takeaway: Batch similar tasks together and protect your transition time: take 2–3 minutes between contexts to reset before starting something new.

cards.title: Deadlines aren't motivators, they're anchors
cards.insight: We often think urgency drives productivity, but deadlines actually anchor our effort to the minimum needed to 'pass.' Without a deadline, we often exceed it; with one, we rarely do.
cards.takeaway: For deep work, set internal milestones 25–30% ahead of the real deadline to create buffer space and room for genuine problem-solving.

cards.title: Friction is the real killer of focus
cards.insight: It's not willpower that fails—it's friction. Every tiny obstacle between you and your task (finding the file, opening the app, finding your notes) drains decision energy. By the time you start, your focus is already compromised.
cards.takeaway: Invest 10 minutes upfront removing friction: organize materials, clear your desk, open all needed apps before you begin the actual work.

cards.title: Boredom is a feature, not a bug
cards.insight: Periods of apparent 'doing nothing'—waiting for coffee, staring out the window—are when your brain consolidates learning and generates novel connections. Filling every gap with stimulation prevents this critical background processing.
cards.takeaway: Protect at least two 5-minute windows per day of genuinely unstimulated time; no phone, no reading—just thinking or observing.

ai.summary: Multiple indicators suggest the AI spending boom may be unsustainable: mounting debt, negative cash flow at major tech firms, and investor skepticism about returns are all raising questions about the long-term viability of the current capex trajectory. Tech companies are being forced to justify billions in data center spending as enthusiasm wanes. The shift reflects a reckoning over whether AI investments will deliver promised returns.
